Anjuna Beach, located on the western coast of India, is renowned for its vibrant coral reefs and rich marine biodiversity. The coral formations along Anjuna Beach are integral to the coastal ecosystem, providing habitat for a myriad of marine species while also contributing to the local economy through tourism and fishing. Recent studies have highlighted the significance of these coral patches in maintaining ecological balance and supporting biodiversity (Kaushik, n.d.). Understanding the elemental composition of these corals is crucial, as it offers insights into their health and resilience against environmental stressors.

Research indicates that calcium (Ca) constitutes a major component of coral skeletons, playing a vital role in their structural integrity. A study utilizing Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) found that coral skeletons from various locations exhibited significant levels of calcium content ranging from 36% to nearly 40% by weight (Haider, n.d.). This high concentration underscores the importance of calcium not only for coral growth but also for resilience against ocean acidification—a pressing issue due to climate change. The findings suggest that monitoring calcium levels can serve as an effective metric for assessing coral health in Anjuna Beach.

Furthermore, interactions between marine organisms at Anjuna Beach illustrate complex ecological relationships. For instance, allelopathic interactions among rocky intertidal species such as *Cinachyrella cf. cavernosa* and *Zoanthus sansibaricus* emphasize how chemical compounds can regulate community dynamics within these ecosystems (Anshika, n.d.). Such interactions are essential for understanding species coexistence and competition in delicate habitats like those found at Anjuna Beach.

Not recommended to visit if you have time constraints.

title: Overpriced parking and goods
location: Kulem Station FOB, Kolem, Goa 403410, India (15.336353, 74.244316)
description: Reviewer reported that parking and basic items were openly overpriced and sold above MRP.
address: Kulem Station FOB, Kolem, Goa 403410, India
review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ for Nature | ⭐ for Management & Authorities
My visit to Dudhsagar Waterfall was honestly disappointing overall, except for the natural beauty. I would not recommend this place unless you are very particular and desperate to visit it.

Tourists are neither valued nor respected here. Everything felt openly overpriced and exploitative. Parking itself costs ₹300, and that too in an unsecured area. Basic items like breakfast, water bottles, and snacks are sold well above MRP, and you are not even allowed to question it.

The safari is arranged by a government setup, but the organizers are least bothered about tourists. Vehicles are arranged purely at their convenience. We had to wait nearly 3 hours in a queue just to get a safari vehicle. Since we had already traveled 2 hours from the Baga beach area, we had no option but to wait.

I was assisting a couple from Singapore, and the local agents were extremely rude and unprofessional. Instead of helping, they told me to “mind my own business” and warned me that this is their locality and we must go by their rules. This behavior was shocking and unacceptable, especially at an international tourist destination.

Yes, the waterfall experience itself is beautiful and powerful, and nature deserves full credit. But the locals and the government authorities managing this place are pathetic in terms of hospitality, crowd management, and respect for visitors.

I would strongly suggest skipping this overhyped destination. A similar or even better waterfall experience can be enjoyed at Jog Falls near Gokarna, with much more affordable, organized, and seamless arrangements. Even beach and nature experiences in Gokarna are far more peaceful and tourist-friendly.

I give 5 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ to nature, but not even 1 star to the people and authorities who are ruining the reputation of this place. Unfortunately, because of such experiences, Goa tourism is getting affected compared to earlier days.

title: Unexpected extra charges for meals

address: Kulem Station FOB, Kolem, Goa 403410, India
review_text:
The Dudhsagar Sagar Trek is great experience and I would suggest to visit the falls by trek as this gives the opportunity to connect with nature.

As far the booking with Castle Rock Adventures is concerned, me and my team did not had a great experience. It was very unpleasant. Post going through few reviews from Google, we contacted Suresh for booking. We tried and negotiated the price for 1200 per person. Post reaching the Kulem Station, we contacted the guide Raju and came to know that food was not part of the price. So we agreed to pay extra 150 per person for lunch and we spent extra money for breakfast. The trek was supposed to begin by 8:30 AM but our guide was delaying because he was waiting for other members. We pushed him and post that we started our trek with another guide. The other guide was good and stayed with us the entire time. During lunch time, we observed that our lunch was spoiled and had to manage with snacks that we had kept with us. Since the lunch was arranged by Raju we questioned him but he was in denial and informed us he cannot do any thing regarding this as his food was fine. So in the end the amount we spent for lunch went for toss. This caused a lot of inconvenience for us. Never expected such kind of service from trek company.

As per my experience, I would suggest to reach the Kulem Station and book the guide there. You can probably negotiate with them. There is a decent restaurant named Durga Restaurant at around 200 meters from Kulem Station. They serve good food for breakfast. For packed lunch, the option provided is Veg Briyani or Veg Fried Rice. You can check with the restaurant as they might be able to help you. Other forest entry charges you can pay directly at check post. If you speak to guide, they will assist you with all the details. Poor Planning and Substandard Infrastructure – A Nightmare for Passengers
I am extremely disappointed with the newly constructed Platform No. 6 at Margao (Madgaon) Railway Station. It is clear that the contract was executed with zero regard for passenger convenience.

Uneven Layout: The platform is not level or equal with the other platforms, making it feel disconnected and poorly integrated into the station.
Missing Coach Indicators: There are no proper displays to show where specific coaches will arrive. Passengers are forced to run blindly when the train pulls in.
Terrible Accessibility: For such a long platform, they have only provided a single lift. Instead of installing escalators for quick movement, they’ve built 100-meter-long ramps.
The "Missed Train" Trap: If a passenger arrives even slightly late, the walk down that long ramp almost guarantees they will miss their train. It is impossible to hurry through this layout with luggage.
It feels like the budget was completely mismanaged or "eaten up" by the contractors. This isn't modern infrastructure; it’s a hurdle race for the common man. The authorities need to look into this corruption and fix these basic amenities immediately.

Beware of Scammers Near Madgaon Railway Station Goa

If you are visiting Goa for the first time, especially through Madgaon Railway Station, please be very careful of the people approaching tourists outside the station offering bike rentals and stays. A person named Adham Raza approached me and convinced me to rent an Activa for ₹500 per day. Since it was my first time in Goa, I trusted them.

Before taking the bike, I clearly asked about the terms and conditions in case of any issue or breakdown. They assured me that if anything happened, I could repair it, show the bill, and they would fully reimburse the amount.

The next day, while traveling from South Goa to North Goa, the bike tyre suddenly became punctured. I had to push the vehicle with heavy luggage to the nearest service center. The mechanic checked the tyre and found no nail or outside damage. Later, we discovered that the tyre itself was already in very poor condition internally. Honestly, it was lucky that the tyre did not burst while riding, otherwise it could have caused a serious accident.

I informed them immediately, repaired the tyre for ₹450 with my own money, and continued my trip after replacing it. The new tyre worked perfectly throughout North Goa and Old Goa, clearly proving the original tyre was already damaged and unsafe.

When I returned the vehicle, they refunded only ₹250 and started arguing aggressively instead of taking responsibility. Their behavior completely changed once a problem happened. They acted rude, arrogant, and intimidating like local gundas.

They also offer stay/accommodation services, so please do not trust them blindly. These people target tourists near Madgaon Railway Station and behave very politely at first just to gain trust. Once you face any issue, they avoid responsibility and try to intimidate customers.

I am attaching photos and booking details so other travelers can stay aware. Please be careful around these scammers near Madgaon Railway Station, Goa.

review_text: Mopa airport is situated far away from the main towns like Mapusa and panaji. unlike other cities like bangalore and Mumbai There is no public transport here. title: Unmarked parking fine policy
description: Reviewer reported being fined for parking due to poorly visible signage regarding time limits.
review_text:
If you’re a first-time visitor, please be aware that cars are only allowed to stop briefly for entry, drop-off and exit. Parking for more than 5 minutes results in a fine of ₹400.

Unfortunately, there are no clearly visible signboards at the entrance to inform visitors about this rule. When I asked about it while paying the fine, I was told that a notice exists, but it was not noticeable at all and may be too small or poorly placed.

While I appreciate the intention behind managing traffic efficiently, there should be proper, visible signage or security personnel informing drivers in advance; similar to the system followed at Bangalore KIA Airport.

My experience felt unfair due to the lack of clear communication and I hope this can be improved for future visitors.

title: Overcharged for drop-off time limit
description: Reviewer was charged an unexpected fee of Rs.210 for overtime in the drop off zone due to hidden rules.
review_text:
Dark pattern alert ⚠️
1. They didn't tell me there was a 5 minute limit for drop off, while entering the drop off zone.

title: Excessive parking fees and policy
description: Reviewer perceived the short parking grace period and high fees as a money-making scheme and passenger harassment.
review_text:
Mopa Airport has turned into a symbol of passenger harassment. Allowing only 5 minutes of free parking and charging ₹210 for just 2 minutes extra clearly shows how unfriendly and money-focused this system has become.
There is no grace period, no proper guidance, and no concern for common people. Everything feels designed to extract money rather than to support travelers.
Under the current Goa government and the leadership of CM Pramod Sawant, it appears that such policies are encouraged, where public infrastructure is treated more like a money-making business than a public service. This kind of governance creates a strong perception of open loot and zero accountability.
Passengers deserve transparency, fairness, and basic respect — not unreasonable charges and frustration. This airport’s management and the authorities responsible need to seriously rethink their priorities.
Extremely disappointing. Worst parking policy. Anti-public approach.

title: Revenue trap and unfair drop-off charges
description: Reviewer claims the drop-off exit policy is a revenue trap and was charged ₹210 due to poor sensor placement.
review_text: Mopa Airport’s 5-minute exit policy is a blatant revenue trap; I was charged ₹210 for a 60-second delay because the timer starts at the outer gate rather than the drop-off zone. Furthermore, the exit sensors are placed way past the roundabout instead of at the end of the drop-off lane, making it impossible to leave on time without rash driving. Authorities must relocate sensors to the actual drop-off points and stop prioritizing profits over passenger safety.

description: Reviewer reported high parking fees and per-hour bed charges enforced by a beach shack.
review_text:

Also they charge Rs50/- per bed per hour and when I went there, no waiver was offered. I will advise to avoid this place not just because of their monopoly but also because they have spoilt the charm of GOA. Please follow the signage boards all through the GOA which will lead you to the actual Morjim Beach instead of this one which is the default search result of Google.
While coming from Calangute, just don't turn right at Beach Cross Junction, instead follow the sign board and continue straight which will lead to the actual beauty of Morjim Beach.

review_text: At the Tivim Junction in North Goa, Railway Police personnel and the operators of the bike stand are colluding to swindle passengers and the public, extracting between ₹1,00,000 and ₹2,00,000 daily. description: Reviewer reported experiencing uncomfortable staring and harassment by men while visiting the lane as a woman.
review_text:
If you’re a girl, I would strongly advise you never to visit Tito’s Lane. The place is extremely overcrowded, and the crowd is honestly cheap and third-class. Men stare at you from head to toe without any shame — it’s creepy, uncomfortable, and downright unsafe.

If you still choose to go, do not wear western outfits. Just cover yourself fully, otherwise you’ll spend the whole time feeling watched and judged.

And the street food? Please avoid it at all costs. Most of it looks stale, unhygienic, and honestly questionable. The shawarma I ate from one of the stalls was rotten, and I ended up with severe food poisoning. Definitely not worth the risk.

Overall: Tito’s Lane is overrated, unsafe, unhygienic, and absolutely not worth visiting — especially for women.
